title: Anyone else min max their monthly sub?
author: Moist_Signal_5080
selftext:
I make sure to use every bit of my weekly usage, never a single percent left. If it’s only a few percentage left for the week, I wait til about 1 hour before my weekly reset and start a task. Gives me enough time to top it off and still continue with the active context after the reset.

Then I also cancel my subscription as soon as I start it. I’ll let it expire then resub at my weekly reset. For example, my renewal date was this past Wednesday. So I used my entirely weekly usage by then, and stopped my subscription. So when Saturday at 5 pm rolls around ( my weekly reset time), I’ll renew it again. Squeezing those extra days will eventually add up to be an extra week/month I’m not paying for.

Yeah I know, pretty excessive.

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body:
Wow, I've honestly never thought of the savings from being unsubscribed for a few days while it resets. What kind of plan are you on?

For me, I always thought it was more economical to just pay them more than to think more about my usage caps. Good for you for squeezing them for a few more pennies, though!

replies.author: Moist_Signal_5080
replies.body: I’m using the $20 Claude plan. I originally did it as a test. I thought if I let it lapse, then resub, I might get an instant reset. That didn’t work, it still locks in your normal reset date. But there seems to be no downside to not being subscribed for those few days. So I figured I’d keep doing it haha.

replies.author: Frequent-Motor-492
replies.body: But why? Don't you just have to re-subscribe? For nothing?

replies.author: Moist_Signal_5080
replies.body: The idea is that it pushes my subscription date a few days forward every month. If I didn’t cancel, I would have been charged for the month already, even though I can’t use it til Saturday. Why begin paying 3 days before I can even utilize it again. It’s very minimal, but also barely any effort on my end.

replies.author: DigitalDustChan
replies.body: I'm on the $200 plan and at that point it's very important to ration your attention because you run out of things you can stand to think about.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
no, because: 

a) there are loyalty rewards for just leaving the subscription active. i'm sketical that shaving tokens off here or there exceeds the monthly discount for leaving the subscription active 

b) i don't want my account to be flagged by customer service as a problematic account that will never be assisted any way in the future because the company wants to get rid of me 

c) my stress levels, health and peace of mind also all have real value and costs attached to them, and constantly trying to micro-manage maximum optimal efficiency into the services i use exhausts my personal resources. again, there's no way the value of micro-managing my $20/month Codex subcription will outweigh the stress that activity causes and the amount of fun it will drain from my life. OpenAI can keep the pennies; I'll take the bedrest

replies.author: Moist_Signal_5080
replies.body: Yeah if it stresses you out that much, it’s absolutely not worth it. I don’t really think about it, just turn off auto renewal after paying. Nothing nefarious or against the rules, no ones required to stay subscribed indefinitely. On the Claude $20 plan, I don’t really have to try to use all my usage in 3-4 days. Quite the opposite actually, I have to try to conserve it if I don’t want to burn through it. So my penny pinching naturally fits into how I do things anyway.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
Just FYI - not judging you or trying to moralize to you, strictly want to inform you in case you don't know - I worked in a call center absolutely ages ago for AT&T, and they 100% had automated systems even back then that flagged accounts that did anything like that. Not against the rules, nothing nefarious, just like you say - but you got a nice little checkmark in company's billing system, and if you needed help and had that checkmark? Nope. We'll sell you a phone, if you want. Beyond that, nope, sorry, can't help.

Company had no ability to get rid of such customers, but found others ways to basically make them quit the service via atrophy.

There is no doubt in my mind that OpenAI and Anthropic and other services have the same idea in their backend, but way more sophisticated and plugged into systems that are far more opaque. Like, the front end of OpenAI doesn't even tell you which imagegen model you're using. They can just downgrade you and you wouldn't know, except suddenly every generation would just suck.

So I'd rather not invite problems from the kitchen I intend to eat from, so to speak. 

Maybe that's overly paranoid or whatever; you do you.
